scenario: Team publishes a new supporting post about 'how to measure email deliverability' and, in the same publishing pass, adds a link to it from the 'Email Marketing Guide' pillar page and from two sibling posts in the cluster, using anchor text 'measuring email deliverability'.
Writer publishes a new cluster post but leaves it unlinked from any other page on the site, planning to add internal links 'later once traffic picks up'.

Editor replaces an anchor text 'click here' pointing to a related post with descriptive anchor text 'our guide to cart-abandonment emails', placed at the point in the article where that guide is actually relevant to the reader.

To boost a target keyword's rankings, a writer inserts the exact-match keyword phrase as anchor text into an internal link even though it reads awkwardly and doesn't match the linked page's actual topic.

Marketer turns a published blog post's key statistics into a five-slide LinkedIn carousel and a short video script, without applying any canonical tag or duplicate-content mitigation to either format.
A published post is cross-posted verbatim as a full article on a partner's blog (a separate indexable web page) with no canonical tag added on either side and no link back to the original.

When adapting a blog post's stat ('conversion rates rose 34% in Q2') into an email newsletter blurb, the writer re-checks the source data before reusing the number, since the number carries over into a new format.

While turning a post into a video script, the scriptwriter changes an attributed customer quote to a rounder, punchier phrasing to fit the video's pacing, without re-verifying the change against the original source.
Before syndicating a post to an industry partner site, the two parties agree the original company blog URL is canonical, and the partner adds a rel="canonical" tag on their copy pointing to that URL.

A partner site republishing a syndicated post cannot technically add a canonical tag, so the publisher requests the partner add a clear, direct link back to the original article as the next-best signal.
After syndicating a post to three partner sites, the original post's own canonical tag is left pointing to one of the syndicated partner URLs instead of to itself.
Before publishing a cluster update, the editor clicks through every new and updated internal link to confirm each one resolves and that anchor text still matches the linked page's current content.
A syndicated copy goes live on a partner site without anyone checking whether its canonical tag actually points to the correct original URL.
